notes.md: - **Mohammedan Literary Society:** founded at **Calcutta in 1863** by **Nawab Abdul Latif** (its secretary) to spread **Western education** and modern ideas among Muslims.

new.s: Which commission recommended abolishing the separate presidency armies, which led to a single Indian Army in 1895?
new.x: The Eden Commission (1879) recommended ending the three presidency armies; a single Indian Army with four commands followed in 1895.
new.angle: U0187 notes gap: Eden Commission -> single Indian Army

new.s: Under which Act was Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India in 1877?
new.x: The Royal Titles Act, 1876 gave Victoria the title Empress of India; she was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar on 1 January 1877.
new.angle: U0187 notes gap: Royal Titles Act 1876

new.s: Who introduced the portfolio system in 1859, which was given statutory recognition by the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
new.x: Canning introduced the portfolio system in 1859, putting each council member in charge of a department; the 1861 Act recognised it.
new.angle: U0187 notes gap: portfolio system -> Canning

new.s: Who was the first Governor-General of India?
new.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; the first was William Bentinck.
new.angle: U0187 notes gap: first GG of India -> Bentinck

new.s: Which organisation was the first to petition against the non-implementation of the Queen's Proclamation of 1858?
new.x: The Madras Native Association (1852), founded by Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, was the first to petition against the non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation.
new.angle: U0187 notes gap: Madras Native Association petition

new.s: Who was the ruler of Bobbili when it was attacked by Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram and the French in 1757?
new.x: Bobbili was defended by Ranga Rao, whose queen was Mallamma Devi; the fort fell to Vizianagaram and Bussy's French troops.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Bobbili defender Ranga Rao

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bobbili (1757):
1. Bobbili was defended by Ranga Rao.
2. The French under Bussy helped Bobbili against Vizianagaram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ranga Rao defended Bobbili; the French under Bussy helped the attacker, Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram, so statement 2 is wrong.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Bobbili defender Ranga Rao

new.s: The Battle of Raichur (1520) is regarded as the greatest battle of which ruler?
new.x: Raichur (1520) was the greatest battle of Sri Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Raichur 1520 -> Krishnadevaraya

new.s: Under which arrangement did the Nizam cede Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary to the Company in 1800?
new.x: The Ceded Districts were handed over in 1800 under the Nizam's Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: cession of 1800 under Subsidiary Alliance

new.s: Veerapandya Kattabomman was the poligar of which place?
new.x: Kattabomman was the poligar of Panchalankurichi in Tirunelveli; he was hanged at Kayattar in 1799.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Kattabomman -> Panchalankurichi

new.s: In which fort was Mubariz-ud-Daula, the leader of the Wahabi Movement of 1839, imprisoned?
new.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula, the Nizam's brother, was arrested and jailed in Golconda Fort.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Mubariz-ud-Daula -> Golconda Fort

new.s: Who led the revolt at Aurangabad in June 1857?
new.x: At Aurangabad the 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent was disarmed and Mir Fida Ali revolted; Captain Abbot suppressed it and Fida Ali was hanged.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Aurangabad 1857 -> Mir Fida Ali

new.s: Who led the rising against the British at Shorapur in 1858?
new.x: In 1858 Raja Venkatappa Nayaka of Shorapur rose against the British, the last of the Hyderabad-region risings in order.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Shorapur 1858 -> Venkatappa Nayaka

new.s: In 1858, Raja Venkatappa Nayaka rose against the British at which place?
new.x: Venkatappa Nayaka was the Raja of Shorapur; his rising of 1858 came after the Hyderabad Residency attack of 1857.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Shorapur 1858 -> Venkatappa Nayaka

new.s: Who inquired into the causes of the Rampa rebellion of 1879?
new.x: Sullivan of the Board of Revenue inquired into the 1879 Rampa rising and found the toddy tax and the mansabdar's oppression as causes.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Rampa 1879 inquiry -> Sullivan

new.s: The hill unrest of the 1830s in the Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam region led to the introduction of which system?
new.x: Unrest against zamindari exactions in the Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam hills in the 1830s led to the Agency system.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: 1830s hill unrest -> Agency system

new.s: Where is Padmanabham, the site of the battle of 1794, located?
new.x: The Battle of Padmanabham (10 July 1794) was fought at Padmanabham, between Bhimunipatnam and Vizianagaram.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Padmanabham location

new.s: What did the Company demand from Chinna Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram, which led to the Battle of Padmanabham?
o: A tribute of Rs 3 lakh and disbanding of his troops
new.x: The Company demanded Rs 3 lakh tribute and the disbanding of troops; the Raja refused, and the fight ended at Padmanabham in 1794.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: Padmanabham cause

new.s: Which was the first big sepoy mutiny in India, about half a century before 1857?
new.x: The Vellore Mutiny of 10 July 1806 was the first big sepoy mutiny, caused by new dress rules and the presence of Tipu's family in the fort.
new.angle: U0188 notes gap: first big sepoy mutiny -> Vellore

new.s: Hindu College, Calcutta (1817), which Rammohan Roy helped David Hare to set up, later became which college?
new.x: Hindu College, India's first Western-style secular college, later became Presidency College.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Hindu College -> Presidency College

new.s: Who was given the title 'Maharishi'?
new.x: 'Maharishi' was the title of Debendranath Tagore, not Rammohan Roy, who was called 'Raja'.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Maharishi -> Debendranath Tagore

new.s: Debendranath Tagore, known as 'Maharishi', was the father of whom?
new.x: Rabindranath Tagore was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore; Dwarkanath Tagore was Debendranath's father.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Maharishi -> Debendranath Tagore

new.s: In which year did the Tattvabodhini Sabha merge into the Brahmo Samaj?
new.x: Debendranath's Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) merged into the Brahmo Samaj in 1859.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Tattvabodhini merger 1859

new.s: Whose lectures in Bombay inspired the founding of the Prarthana Samaj?
new.x: Keshab Chandra Sen took the Brahmo message to the south; his Bombay lectures inspired the Prarthana Samaj (1867).
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Keshab -> Prarthana Samaj

new.s: Who founded the first Prarthana Samaj in Andhra at Rajahmundry in 1878?
new.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam set up the first Prarthana Samaj centre in Andhra at Rajahmundry in 1878.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: first Andhra Prarthana Samaj

new.s: In which year was the first Prarthana Samaj in Andhra founded at Rajahmundry?
new.x: Veeresalingam founded it at Rajahmundry in 1878, eleven years after the Bombay Prarthana Samaj (1867).
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: first Andhra Prarthana Samaj

new.s: With which reformer is the Seva Sadan associated?
new.x: The Seva Sadan is correctly paired with Malabari; Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj and Agnihotri the Dev Samaj.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Seva Sadan -> Malabari

new.s: Who led the Faraizi Movement?
new.x: The Faraizi Movement of Bengal was led by Haji Shariatullah.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Faraizi -> Haji Shariatullah

new.s: Who was the first editor of the Bengali weekly Som Prakash (1858)?
new.x: Som Prakash was Vidyasagar's idea, but its first editor was Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan.
new.angle: U0189 notes gap: Som Prakash editor

new.s: What was the main aim of the Aligarh Movement?
o: Distribution of land to the landless
new.x: The Aligarh Movement worked for modern (Western) education among Muslims; Deoband stood for religious education.
new.angle: U0190 notes gap: Aligarh Movement aim

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Body)
A. Arya Samaj
B. Satyashodhak Samaj
C. Sharada Sadan
D. Prarthana Samaj
List-II (Work)
1. Home for widows
2. True knowledge of the Vedas
3. Improvement of women and depressed classes
4. Justice for untouchables
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Arya Samaj - Vedas; Satyashodhak Samaj - untouchables; Pandita Ramabai's Sharada Sadan - widows; Prarthana Samaj - women and depressed classes.
new.angle: U0190 notes gap: body -> work match

new.s: Who founded the Mohammedan Literary Society at Calcutta in 1863?
new.x: Nawab Abdul Latif founded the Mohammedan Literary Society at Calcutta in 1863 and was its secretary.
new.angle: U0190 web: Mohammedan Literary Society founder (PYQ yacc3eed0e07 angle)

new.s: What was the main aim of the Mohammedan Literary Society founded by Nawab Abdul Latif in 1863?
o: Spreading Western education and modern ideas among Muslims
new.x: Founded at Calcutta in 1863, it sought to reawaken Muslims through Western education and modern ideas.
new.angle: U0190 web: Mohammedan Literary Society aim

new.s: Who is called the 'Grandfather of the Indian Nation'?
new.x: Dayananda Saraswati is called the 'Grandfather of the Indian Nation'; Lajpat Rai also called him the 'Martin Luther of India'.
new.angle: U0191 notes gap: Grandfather of the Indian Nation

new.s: Which of the following titles is NOT associated with Dayananda Saraswati?
new.x: 'Prophet of Indian Nationalism' is a title of Swami Vivekananda; the others belong to Dayananda.
new.angle: U0191 notes gap: Grandfather of the Indian Nation

new.s: At which event in New Delhi in November 2025 were the 200th birth anniversary of Dayananda Saraswati and 150 years of the Arya Samaj marked?
new.x: The International Arya Mahasammelan 2025 (Jnana Jyoti Festival), New Delhi, marked Dayananda's 200th birth anniversary and 150 years of the Arya Samaj.
new.angle: U0191 notes gap: Arya Mahasammelan 2025

new.s: How many principles did Dayananda Saraswati draft for the Arya Samaj?
new.x: Dayananda drafted the Ten Principles of the Arya Samaj, stressing truth, the Vedas and the welfare of all.
new.angle: U0191 notes gap: Ten Principles

new.s: In which year did Munshi Ram set up the Gurukul Kangri near Haridwar?
new.x: After the 1893 split, Munshi Ram (later Swami Shraddhanand) of the Gurukul party set up Gurukul Kangri in 1902.
new.angle: U0191 notes gap: Gurukul Kangri 1902

new.s: Which of the following was the first Central University (set up under a central Act)?
new.x: BHU (1916) was the first Central University; Calcutta, Madras and Bombay (1857) were affiliating universities.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: first Central University -> BHU

new.s: In which year did Annie Besant come to India?
new.x: Annie Besant joined the Theosophical Society in 1889 and came to India in 1893.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Besant came to India 1893

new.s: In which year did Annie Besant start the Home Rule League?
new.x: Besant started the Home Rule League in 1916, the same year she founded the BT College at Madanapalle.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Besant Home Rule League 1916

new.s: Which reformer is credited as the first to urge Swadeshi and the boycott of foreign goods?
new.x: Dayanand Saraswati is credited as the first to urge Swadeshi and boycott of foreign goods, and the first to use the term 'Swaraj'.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: first to urge Swadeshi -> Dayanand

new.s: Who wrote 'Gulamgiri'?
new.x: Jyotiba Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), wrote Gulamgiri and Sarvajanik Satyadharm Pustak.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Gulamgiri -> Phule

new.s: Where was the Nadwah-ul-Ulama founded in 1894?
new.x: The Nadwah-ul-Ulama was founded at Lucknow in 1894.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Nadwah-ul-Ulama -> Lucknow

new.s: Who wrote the Bengali play Neel Darpan (1860) on the plight of indigo farmers?
new.x: Neel Darpan (1860) was written by Dinabandhu Mitra; Michael Madhusudan Dutta translated it into English.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Neel Darpan -> Dinabandhu Mitra

new.s: Who translated Dinabandhu Mitra's Neel Darpan into English?
new.x: The English translation of Neel Darpan, the play on indigo farmers, was made by Michael Madhusudan Dutta.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: Neel Darpan -> Dinabandhu Mitra

new.s: Who started the Bengal Gazette (1780), the first newspaper in India?
new.x: The Bengal Gazette, India's first newspaper, was started by J.A. Hicky in 1780.
new.angle: U0192 notes gap: first newspaper -> Hicky
